A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LexRel and its civil legal relation schema. All pages, including figures and appendices, support comparison. The original appendix prompt tables are retained unchanged in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations, downstream task experiments, evaluator validation, and analysis of legal relation distributions in Sections 5.1–5.3.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and reports revised downstream experiments, annotator agreement, and extraction error analyses.

M1.justification: The schema, two-stage type/argument extraction, expert-corrected annotation pipeline, supervised distillation, and relation-augmented inference remain unchanged. Revised explanations and downstream applications do not establish a different method.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 replaces Document Proofreading and Statute Prediction with Case Analysis and Criminal Damages Calculation, retaining Consultation. This substantially changes downstream task requirements, including numerical damages calculation. LexRel and the litigation-distribution corpus remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 4 replaces InternLM3-8B with Qwen3-8B, including on the retained Consultation task. GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and MiniCPM4-8B remain. Table 3 retains its entire comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces a separate agreement-assessment protocol using 300 randomly sampled instances, independent annotations, and senior-expert review/adjudication. The existing 60-item/193-pair evaluator validation, 5,500 training samples, and main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C substantially expands diagnostic analysis through legal/social relation confusion, long-tail misclassification, object misidentification, and content omission, with representative cases in Figures 4–7 and quantified confusion frequencies. Appendix B adds annotation-quality validation. The existing long-tail analysis is retained.

E5.justification: v2 first reports inter-annotator agreement using Cohen’s kappa on 300 instances. Existing t-test significance reporting and the chi-square/Cramér’s V analysis are unchanged; no additional seed or repeated-run reporting appears.

E6.justification: Table 4 replaces most downstream results and adds Qwen3-8B Consultation scores of 15.0 without relations and 14.2 with relations. Appendices add kappa 0.706 and confusion frequencies of 81.1% for Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and 28.6% for o3-mini. Table 3 is unchanged; shared Consultation scores differ only by rounding.

T1.justification: The formal task definitions in Equations 1–2 and the schema’s argument definitions remain unchanged. v2 introduces no new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The contribution list drops the claim that LexRel is the first expert-annotated benchmark for this task. The first comprehensive schema claim and central conclusions about extraction difficulty and downstream benefits remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds substantive explanations of overgeneralization, insufficient exposure to rare relations, and missing legal detail. Section 7 newly acknowledges DeepSeek model-family coupling between training-data generation and evaluation. Section 5.3 revises downstream mechanisms and discusses usefulness despite imperfect extraction.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised release upon acceptance with a stated data/code repository link. It removes attachment-folder instructions and the explicit vLLM, Llama-Factory, and SFT configuration-file description. Hardware information and prompt templates remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Joshi et al. and Santosh et al., acknowledging prior event/relation representations for retrieval and summarization. Agreement-related references to Cohen and Landis–Koch are added, while the Llama-Factory reference is removed.

P1.justification: v2 polishes wording across the abstract, introduction, construction, and experimental sections while retaining the main narrative structure. It updates author/contact text, adds acknowledgments, and reorganizes the appendices, moving Prompts from Appendix C to A.

P2.justification: Figures 4–7 add a substantial visual error-analysis component with factual text, gold answers, and incorrect outputs. Table 4 has revised headings, rules, and numerical formatting; Figure 1 receives small spacing adjustments. The unchanged prompt tables move later in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The new agreement assessment and concrete failure cases improve transparency beyond v1’s aggregate evaluations. The model-family coupling limitation and repository pointer also help readers assess and access the work. These gains are limited: core extraction evidence is unchanged, the agreement procedure leaves adjudication effects unclear, and some implementation documentation is removed.
